Below is a minimal pattern that works well for React sites. ```python import asyncio from crawl4ai import AsyncWebCrawler, CrawlerRunConfig, BrowserConfig from crawl4ai.async_configs import CacheMode async def main(): run_config = CrawlerRunConfig( cache_mode=CacheMode.BYPASS, # Good defaults for JS-heavy SPAs: scan_full_page=True, # scrolls page to trigger lazy loads (see lazy-loading docs) scroll_delay=0.5, wait_for_images=True, # wait until images are actually loaded verbose=True, ) browser_config = BrowserConfig( headless=True, # set False for debugging # you can add timeout / viewport options here if needed ) async with AsyncWebCrawler(config=browser_config) as crawler: result = await crawler.arun("https://your-react-site.com", config=run_config) if not result.success: print("Error:", result.error_message) return # React-rendered content will be in result.html / result.cleaned_html / result.fit_html print(result.html[:2000]) # raw final DOM print("Links:", len(result.links.get("internal", []))) print("Images:", len(result.media.get("images", []))) asyncio.run(main()) ``` Relevant pieces from the docs: - `wait_for_images=True` makes the crawler “ensure images have finished loading before finalizing the HTML”.
